verses.text: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my spice. I have eaten my honeycomb and my honey. I have drunk my wine and my milk. The friends say: Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink your fill of love.
I was asleep, but my heart was awake. Listen! My beloved is knocking: "Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my perfect one. My head is wet with dew, and my hair with the damp of the night."
I have taken off my robe. Must I put it on again? I have washed my feet. Must I get them dirty again?
My beloved put his hand through the opening of the latch, and my heart pounded for him.
I got up to open the door for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with flowing myrrh, on the handles of the lock.
I opened the door for my beloved, but my beloved had turned and gone away. My heart sank when he spoke. I looked for him, but I did not find him. I called him, but he did not answer.
The watchmen who go around the city found me. They beat me and bruised me. The guards of the walls took away my cloak.
Daughters of Jerusalem, I make you promise: if you find my beloved, tell him that I am weak with love.
How is your beloved better than any other, most beautiful of women? How is your beloved better than any other, that you make us promise this?
My beloved is fair and glowing with health, the best among ten thousand.
His head is like the purest gold. His hair is wavy and black as a raven.
His eyes are like doves beside streams of water, washed in milk, set like jewels.
His cheeks are like beds of spices, giving off sweet perfume. His lips are like lilies, dripping with flowing myrrh.
His arms are like rods of gold set with jewels. His body is like polished ivory covered with sapphires.
His legs are like marble pillars set on bases of fine gold. He looks like Lebanon, as fine as its cedars.
His mouth is sweetness itself. Yes, he is lovely in every way. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, daughters of Jerusalem.
